red_flags.detail: SCOUT.md gives T's |P_lead| >= 4 and F(T) >= 6; WORK.md (the later, more refined pass in the same directory) gives |P_lead| >= 5 and F(T) >= 7 for the same object T. Both numbers stand side by side in the same arc directory with no cross-reference marking the SCOUT.md figures as superseded by the WORK.md figures, though the conclusion (refutation) is unaffected either way.

The cell's own FINDINGS.md/arc_verdict.json record verdict OPEN and describe this as scouting-only with 'no verdict claimed against any criterion', but SCOUT.md's headline explicitly makes a strong recommendation ('L137 should be CLOSED... because the post-hoc observation it registers is REFUTED') and WORK.md issues an even sharper one ('CLOSE L137 AS UNSEALABLE'). The verdict file's text is technically consistent (scouting produces recommendations, not seals) but a reader skimming only arc_verdict.json would not learn that a full refutation argument, with a named counterexample (T), sits underneath.

arcs.seat_note: This is an unusually self-critical worker cell: it independently reproduces B947's own verdict from source before using it, names and computes an explicit counterexample (T) against the club's headline 'value/pencil' story, and flags its own gauge-dependence and computability problems rather than papering over them -- a genuine methodological positive. But it is purely arithmetic (cubic-field factorisation classification), carries no measurable physical quantity or prediction, and its status is muddied by an OPEN verdict file that undersells the strength of the refutation argument actually present in SCOUT.md/WORK.md.
